# Method A: Excel Import

Uses `scripts/generate_zephyr_test_cases.py` to fetch ACs from Jira and produce a
Zephyr-native Excel file that creates Test issues, populates steps, and sets the
"is a test for" link in a single import operation.

## Step 1: Generate the Excel file

```bash
python3 scripts/generate_zephyr_test_cases.py PROJ-XXXX PROJ-YYYY
# Output: reports/test-cases-proj-xxxx-proj-yyyy.xlsx
```

Requires `JIRA_SERVER_TOKEN` (or `JIRA_TOKEN`) env var set to a PAT. Uses the
standard Jira REST API — no ZAPI password needed.

The script:
- Fetches each story and parses AC and Testing Notes lines automatically
- Produces an Excel with `Name`, `Step`, `Testdata`, `Result`, `Priority`, `Labels`,
  `Description`, `Issue Link Type`, `Issues Key To Link` columns
- One row per step; `Name` repeated on every row of the same test case

## Step 2: Import into Zephyr

1. Zephyr top nav → **Tests → Import**
2. Project: `<Your Project Name>` | Issue Type: `Test` | File Type: `Excel`
3. Upload the generated file
4. Discriminator: **By Testcase Name Change** | Starting Row: **2**
5. Map columns (first time only — then **Save Mapping** as `<Project> Zephyr Import`):

| Issue Field | Excel Column |
|-------------|-------------|
| Name \* | Name |
| Step \* | Step |
| Result \* | Result |
| Testdata \* | Testdata |
| Priority | Priority |
| Labels | Labels |
| Description | Description |
| Issue Link Type... | Issue Link Type |
| Issues Key To L... | Issues Key To Link |

\* These auto-map when header names match exactly.

6. Click **Import**. Zephyr creates one Test issue per story with steps populated
   and "is a test for" link set to the parent story.
7. Add Test issues to the Sprint test cycle in Zephyr.
8. Post a testing progress comment on each Story (see Step 3 below).

> **Saved mapping:** After mapping once, click **Save Mapping** → `<Project> Zephyr Import`.
> Future imports use **Retrieve Mapping** — no remapping needed.

> **Re-import warning:** Delete existing Test issues before re-importing the same
> stories, or Zephyr will create duplicates.

---

## Step 3: Post a testing progress comment on each Story

Record the Test issue key(s) returned by the import, then post a comment on each Story using the Jira MCP. The comment format has two states:

**State A - Initial (tests created, not yet executed):**

```
*Test case created for this story (Sprint N):*

|| Test Key || Summary || ACs Covered || Status ||
| [PROJ-XXXX|<url>] | Tests: <story summary> | AC01, AC02, AC03, AC04 | ⬜ Unexecuted |

Test linked to this story via the "Tests" ("is tested by") issue link.
Test added to Sprint N cycle in Zephyr.

_Generated by the create-zephyr-tests skill, {date}_
```

**State B - After execution (update the comment once tests are run):**

Use `mcp_jira_edit_comment` to update the existing comment. Replace the status column and add an Evidence section and Outstanding checklist:

```
*Test case created and executed for this story (Sprint N):*

|| Test Key || Summary || ACs Covered || Status ||
| [PROJ-XXXX|<url>] | Tests: <story summary> | AC01, AC02, AC03, AC04 | ✅ Pass |

Test passed in Sprint N cycle. Linked to story via the "Tests" ("is tested by") issue link.

*Evidence:*
- AC01: <brief description of evidence, e.g. screenshot attached to test issue>
- AC02: <Actions run URL> - <what it showed>
- AC03: <failed run URL> - <error>; <passing run URL> - "All checks passed!"
- AC04: <brief description, e.g. screenshot attached to test issue>

*Outstanding before story can be closed:*
# <any remaining items, e.g. PR merged to main>

_Updated by the create-zephyr-tests skill, {date}_
```

> If any ACs need a screenshot as evidence, note `(screenshot attached to test issue)` in the Evidence section and remind the user to attach it directly to the Zephyr Test issue before marking it as passed.

---

## Step 4: Output pytest marker stub (optional)

If the story will have automated pytest tests, output the marker to add once the test is written:

```python
# Add this marker to your pytest test class or method:

@pytest.mark.jira("PROJ-123")       # Story
@pytest.mark.zephyr("PROJ-456")     # Test issue key
class TestRunLinterWorkflow:
    def test_ac01_...(self): ...
    def test_ac02_...(self): ...
```

This output is informational only. Use the `api-tests` skill to scaffold the actual test file.
